@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# seed-refactor-tasks.sh — cycle-130 refactor task seeder (SDD §5.14, Sprint 259 Task 2.3)
+#
+# Turns Loa refactor commits into candidate refactor tasks for the ablation
+# suite. Lists the commits since DATE whose subject starts with `refactor`,
+# `chore`, `style` or `perf`, that touch at least two source files, all under
+# the allowed roots, and NO test file (a path under a `tests/` directory,
+# `test_*.py`, `*_test.py` or `*.bats`; such a commit is skipped with the
+# reason); refuses by name any candidate touching .claude/, CLAUDE.md,
+# .loa.config.yaml, grimoires/ or .run/. For each selected candidate (the
+# first N, newest first) it writes <out>/tasks/refactor-NN/ (next free number):
+#   fixture/    from the PARENT commit: the touched source files, the other
+#               non-test files in their directories, the tests
+#               under the allowed roots that name a touched file (its basename,
+#               or a Python module's stem; at most 20), and their infrastructure
+#               (conftest.py up to the root, __init__.py, *.bash and *helper*
+#               files beside each test, root runner configs) — a plain tree
+#   hidden/     reference.patch = the commit's diff (a/ b/ prefixes, patch -p1),
+#               manifest.json {"files": []} until the structural check exists
+#   task.yaml   source {kind: loa-history, fix_commit, base_commit, date,
+#               churn: {files, insertions, deletions}} (git diff --numstat of
+#               the commit); test_command = the covering tests; structural_check
+#               null — the structural assertion is authored BY HAND (then listed
+#               in manifest.json and set in structural_check; validate-suite.sh
+#               refuses a refactor task without one)
+#   TASK.md     the subject line and the test command; never the diff
+# The proof — the fixture's own covering tests green at base AND green with
+# the reference patch, run under `env -i PATH HOME=<fresh tmp> LC_ALL=C` plus
+# PYTHONUSERBASE and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 — and a clean
+# evals/graders/no-secrets.sh scan come before the task is moved into place.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   seed-refactor-tasks.sh --since DATE [--select N] --out DIR [--repo DIR]
+#                          [--paths CSV] [--suite-version N] [--dry-run]
+#
+#   options as seed-bugfix-tasks.sh (--select default 4; a commit without a
+#   covering test is skipped and does not count); LOA_SEED_BATS likewise
+#
+# Output (stdout, one line each):
+#   candidate <sha12> <date> <subject>
+#   refused <sha12>: <path>
+#   skipped <sha12>: <reason>          (touches a test file: <path> | touches N
+#                                       source file(s), want at least 2 | …)
+#   proof refactor-NN <sha12>: green at base (N passed) / green at reference (M passed)
+#   churn refactor-NN: files F, insertions I, deletions D
+#   todo refactor-NN: author the structural check …
+#   proof-failed <sha12>: <reason>
+#   wrote <dir>
+#   seed-refactor: C candidate(s), R refused, S skipped; selected X, written W, proof failed F
+#
+# Exit: 0 done; 1 a selected candidate failed its proof; 2 usage.
+# Tested by evals/tests/seed-refactor.bats.
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+
+usage() { sed -n '2,/^# =====.*$/p' "$0" | sed '1d;$d' | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit "${1:-2}"; }
+for a in "$@"; do [[ "$a" == "--help" || "$a" == "-h" ]] && usage 0; done
+[[ $# -gt 0 ]] || usage 2
+for tool in git python3; do command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "seed-refactor: missing tool: $tool" >&2; exit 2; }; done
+
+exec python3 -I "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/seed_tasks.py" refactor --repo-default "$REPO_ROOT" \
+  --no-secrets "$REPO_ROOT/evals/graders/no-secrets.sh" "$@"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# seed-refactor-tasks.sh — cycle-130 refactor task seeder (SDD §5.14, Sprint 259 Task 2.3)
+#
+# Turns Loa refactor commits into candidate refactor tasks for the ablation
+# suite. Lists the commits since DATE whose subject starts with `refactor`,
+# `chore`, `style` or `perf`, that touch at least two source files, all under
+# the allowed roots, and NO test file (a path under a `tests/` directory,
+# `test_*.py`, `*_test.py` or `*.bats`; such a commit is skipped with the
+# reason); refuses by name any candidate touching .claude/, CLAUDE.md,
+# .loa.config.yaml, grimoires/ or .run/. For each selected candidate (the
+# first N, newest first) it writes <out>/tasks/refactor-NN/ (next free number):
+#   fixture/    from the PARENT commit: the touched source files, the other
+#               non-test files in their directories, the tests
+#               under the allowed roots that name a touched file (its basename,
+#               or a Python module's stem; at most 20), and their infrastructure
+#               (conftest.py up to the root, __init__.py, *.bash and *helper*
+#               files beside each test, root runner configs) — a plain tree
+#   hidden/     reference.patch = the commit's diff (a/ b/ prefixes, patch -p1),
+#               manifest.json {"files": []} until the structural check exists
+#   task.yaml   source {kind: loa-history, fix_commit, base_commit, date,
+#               churn: {files, insertions, deletions}} (git diff --numstat of
+#               the commit); test_command = the covering tests; structural_check
+#               null — the structural assertion is authored BY HAND (then listed
+#               in manifest.json and set in structural_check; validate-suite.sh
+#               refuses a refactor task without one)
+#   TASK.md     the subject line and the test command; never the diff
+# The proof — the fixture's own covering tests green at base AND green with
+# the reference patch, run under `env -i PATH HOME=<fresh tmp> LC_ALL=C` plus
+# PYTHONUSERBASE and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 — and a clean
+# evals/graders/no-secrets.sh scan come before the task is moved into place.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   seed-refactor-tasks.sh --since DATE [--select N] --out DIR [--repo DIR]
+#                          [--paths CSV] [--suite-version N] [--dry-run]
+#
+#   options as seed-bugfix-tasks.sh (--select default 4; a commit without a
+#   covering test is skipped and does not count); LOA_SEED_BATS likewise
+#
+# Output (stdout, one line each):
+#   candidate <sha12> <date> <subject>
+#   refused <sha12>: <path>
+#   skipped <sha12>: <reason>          (touches a test file: <path> | touches N
+#                                       source file(s), want at least 2 | …)
+#   proof refactor-NN <sha12>: green at base (N passed) / green at reference (M passed)
+#   churn refactor-NN: files F, insertions I, deletions D
+#   todo refactor-NN: author the structural check …
+#   proof-failed <sha12>: <reason>
+#   wrote <dir>
+#   seed-refactor: C candidate(s), R refused, S skipped; selected X, written W, proof failed F
+#
+# Exit: 0 done; 1 a selected candidate failed its proof; 2 usage.
+# Tested by evals/tests/seed-refactor.bats.
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+
+usage() { sed -n '2,/^# =====.*$/p' "$0" | sed '1d;$d' | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit "${1:-2}"; }
+for a in "$@"; do [[ "$a" == "--help" || "$a" == "-h" ]] && usage 0; done

+for tool in git python3; do command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "seed-refactor: missing tool: $tool" >&2; exit 2; }; done

+exec python3 -I "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/seed_tasks.py" refactor --repo-default "$REPO_ROOT" \
+  --no-secrets "$REPO_ROOT/evals/graders/no-secrets.sh" "$@"

   342	def covering_tests(repo, parent, sources, roots):
   343	    """Test files at parent (under the roots) that name a touched source file."""
   344	    names = set()
   345	    for s in sources:
   346	        base = os.path.basename(s)
   347	        names.add(base)
   348	        if base.endswith(".py"):
   349	            names.add(base[:-3])
   350	    pats = [re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])" + re.escape(n) + r"(?![A-Za-z0-9_])") for n in sorted(names)]
   351	    hits = []
   352	    for r in roots:
   353	        for f in tree_files(repo, parent, r):
   354	            if not is_test(f) or runner_of(f) is None or not safe_path(f) or mount_owned(f):
   355	                continue
   356	            b = blob(repo, parent, f)
   357	            if b is None or b[0] == "120000":
   358	                continue
   359	            text = b[1].decode("utf-8", "replace")
   360	            if any(p.search(text) for p in pats):
   361	                hits.append(f)
   362	    return sorted(set(hits))[:MAX_COVERING_TESTS]

     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# ablation-grade.sh — the cycle-130 ablation grader (SDD §3.6, §5.7, D-4.7, D-4.8;
     4	# PRD FR-6 AC-6.1/6.2/6.4; DEC-0401, DEC-0413, DEC-0414, DEC-0420, DEC-0491, DEC-0493)
     5	#
     6	# Grades ONE run directory written by pipeline-run.sh against its task and writes
     7	# grade.json (the input ablation-row.sh joins into the runs.jsonl row), or
     8	# self-checks a task (--self-check) on a synthetic run built from the task itself.
     9	#
    10	# Usage:
    11	#   ablation-grade.sh <run-dir> <task-id> [--suite-root DIR] [--tasks-dir tasks|smoke]
    12	#                     [--out FILE] [--json] [--executor container|host]
    13	#                     [--image loa-ablation:258] [--docker-bin D]
    14	#                     [--allow-unfrozen] [--allow-partial]
    15	#   ablation-grade.sh --self-check base|reference|noisy --task-yaml F [--suite-root DIR]
    16	#                     [--executor …] [--image …] [--docker-bin D] [--json]
    17	#                     [--allow-unfrozen] [--allow-partial]
    18	#
    19	# Options:
    20	#   --suite-root DIR   suite root (default grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0; with
    21	#                      --self-check, the directory two levels above the task dir)
    22	#   --tasks-dir T      tasks (default) or smoke: the task is <root>/<T>/<task-id>/
    23	#   --out FILE         where grade.json goes (default <run-dir>/grade.json)
    24	#   --json             also print grade.json (self-check: the verdict object) on stdout
    25	#   --executor MODE    container (default; DEC-0491) or host
    26	#   --image IMG        the grading image (default loa-ablation:258)
    27	#   --docker-bin D     docker CLI (default $EVAL_DOCKER_BIN, else docker)
    28	#   --allow-unfrozen   grade although freeze.sh --check fails or the suite has no
    29	#                      MANIFEST.sha256 yet (task authoring only); grade.json records
    30	#                      suite_frozen: false. Without it a drift is exit 2 (DEC-0414).
    31	#   --allow-partial    passed to freeze.sh --check (fewer than four tasks per type)
    32	#   --self-check MODE  base | reference | noisy (noisy: review-catch only), see below
    33	#   --task-yaml F      the task to self-check (<root>/<tasks|smoke>/<id>/task.yaml)
    34	#
    35	# Reads ONLY (DEC-0413): <run-dir>/sandbox/, <run-dir>/snapshots/{index.json,<LABEL>.bundle},
    36	# <run-dir>/transcripts/events-*.jsonl, <run-dir>/eval/adversarial-{review,audit}.json,

    38	# MANIFEST.sha256 (through freeze.sh) and, for review-catch, the key manifest the task
    39	# names (review_catch.manifest) and its PR fixture (self-check only). It never reads

   271	def copy_tree(src, dst, top_exclude=frozenset()):
   272	    """regular files, directories and symlinks only; caches dropped"""
   273	    os.makedirs(dst, exist_ok=True)
   274	    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(src, followlinks=False):
   275	        rel = os.path.relpath(root, src)
   276	        keep = []
   277	        for d in sorted(dirs):
   278	            if (rel == "." and d in top_exclude) or d in EXCLUDE_ANY:
   279	                continue
   280	            sp = os.path.join(root, d)
   281	            dp = os.path.join(dst, rel, d)
   282	            if os.path.islink(sp):
   283	                os.symlink(os.readlink(sp), dp)
   284	                continue
   285	            os.makedirs(dp, exist_ok=True)
   286	            keep.append(d)
   287	        dirs[:] = keep
   288	        for f in sorted(files):
   289	            if rel == "." and f in top_exclude:
   290	                continue
   291	            sp, dp = os.path.join(root, f), os.path.join(dst, rel, f)
   292	            st = os.lstat(sp)
   293	            if stat.S_ISLNK(st.st_mode):
   294	                os.symlink(os.readlink(sp), dp)
   295	            elif stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):

   533	def def_line(tree, path, func, cache):
   534	    if path not in cache:
   535	        try:
   536	            cache[path] = open(os.path.join(tree, path), encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read().splitlines()
   537	        except OSError:
   538	            cache[path] = []
   539	    rx = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:async\s+)?def\s+" + re.escape(func) + r"\s*\(")
   540	    for i, l in enumerate(cache[path], 1):
   541	        if rx.match(l):

   546	def parse_pytest(out, tree):
   547	    lines = out.splitlines()
   548	    summary = None
   549	    for l in reversed(lines):
   550	        m = SUMMARY_RX.match(l.strip())
   551	        if m:
   552	            summary = {k: int(n) for n, k in COUNT_RX.findall(m.group(1))}
   553	            break
   554	    if summary is None:
   555	        return None
   556	    norm = {}
   557	    for k, v in summary.items():
   558	        k = {"error": "errors", "warning": "warnings"}.get(k, k)
   559	        norm[k] = norm.get(k, 0) + v
   560	    outcomes, coll_err = {}, []
   561	    for l in lines:
   562	        m = OUTCOME_RX.match(l)
   563	        if not m:
   564	            continue
   565	        kind, node = m.group(1), m.group(2)
   566	        if kind == "ERROR" and "::" not in node:
   567	            coll_err.append(node)
   568	            continue
   569	        prev = outcomes.get(node)
   570	        bad = kind in ("FAILED", "ERROR")
   571	        outcomes[node] = "bad" if (bad or prev == "bad") else "ok"
   572	    cache = {}
   573	    expanded = 0
   574	    for f in coll_err:
   575	        try:
   576	            text = open(os.path.join(tree, f), encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
   577	        except OSError:
   578	            continue
   579	        for fn in re.findall(r"(?m)^\s*(?:async\s+)?def\s+(test\w*)\s*\(", text):
   580	            outcomes.setdefault(f"{f}::{fn}", "bad")
   581	            expanded += 1
   582	
   583	    def key(node):
   584	        path, _, rest = node.partition("::")
   585	        func = rest.split("::")[-1].split("[")[0]
   586	        return (path, def_line(tree, path, func, cache), node)
   587	    order = sorted(outcomes, key=key)
   588	    total = sum(norm.get(k, 0) for k in ("passed", "failed", "errors", "skipped", "xfailed", "xpassed"))
   589	    total = total - len(coll_err) + expanded
   590	    passed = norm.get("passed", 0)
   591	    if total <= 0 and passed == 0:
   592	        return None
   593	    return {"passed": passed, "total": max(total, len(order)), "order": order,
   594	            "bad": {n for n, v in outcomes.items() if v == "bad"}}

   597	TAP_RX = re.compile(r"^(not )?ok (\d+)\b ?(?:- )?(.*)$")

   600	def parse_tap(out):
   601	    plan, seen = None, {}
   602	    for l in out.splitlines():
   603	        m = re.match(r"^1\.\.(\d+)", l)
   604	        if m and plan is None:
   605	            plan = int(m.group(1))
   606	            continue
   607	        m = TAP_RX.match(l)
   608	        if m:
   609	            n = int(m.group(2))
   610	            desc = re.sub(r"\s+#\s*(?:skip|SKIP|todo|TODO).*$", "", m.group(3)).strip()
   611	            seen[n] = (m.group(1) is None, desc or f"#{n}")
   612	    if plan is None and not seen:
   613	        return None
   614	    total = plan if plan is not None else len(seen)
   615	    if total == 0:
   616	        return None
   617	    nums = sorted(set(range(1, total + 1)) | set(seen))
   618	    names = {n: (seen[n][1] if n in seen else f"#{n}") for n in nums}
   619	    order = [names[n] for n in nums]
   620	    bad = {names[n] for n in nums if n not in seen or not seen[n][0]}
   621	    return {"passed": sum(1 for n in seen if seen[n][0]), "total": total, "order": order, "bad": bad}

   719	def churn(a, b):
   720	    def listing(root):
   721	        out = {}
   722	        for r, ds, fs in os.walk(root, followlinks=False):
   723	            ds[:] = [d for d in ds if d not in EXCLUDE_ANY and not os.path.islink(os.path.join(r, d))]
   724	            for name in fs + [d for d in os.listdir(r) if os.path.islink(os.path.join(r, d)) and os.path.isdir(os.path.join(r, d))]:
   725	                p = os.path.join(r, name)
   726	                out[os.path.relpath(p, root)] = p
   727	        return out
   728	    def content(p):
   729	        if os.path.islink(p):
   730	            return ("link:" + os.readlink(p)).encode()
   731	        try:
   732	            return open(p, "rb").read()
   733	        except OSError:
   734	            return b""
   735	    def lines(bs):
   736	        try:
   737	            return bs.decode("utf-8").splitlines()
   738	        except UnicodeDecodeError:
   739	            return None
   740	    la, lb = listing(a), listing(b)
   741	    files = diff = 0
   742	    for rel in sorted(set(la) | set(lb)):
   743	        ca = content(la[rel]) if rel in la else None
   744	        cb = content(lb[rel]) if rel in lb else None
   745	        if ca == cb:
   746	            continue
   747	        files += 1
   748	        xa = lines(ca) if ca is not None else []
   749	        xb = lines(cb) if cb is not None else []
   750	        if xa is None or xb is None:
   751	            continue
   752	        for l in difflib.unified_diff(xa, xb, lineterm="", n=0):
   753	            if l.startswith(("+++", "---", "@@")):
   754	                continue
   755	            if l.startswith(("+", "-")):
   756	                diff += 1
   757	    return diff, files

   600	def parse_tap(out):

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# evals/tests/seed-bugfix.bats — cycle-130 Sprint 259 Task 2.2 (SDD §5.14,
# sprint AC-2.9)
#
# seed-bugfix-tasks.sh over a throwaway git repo: a clean fix commit (a Python
# module + its test, red at the parent, green at the commit) becomes a task
# whose every field validates; a fix touching .claude/ is refused by name and
# writes nothing; --dry-run writes nothing; a fix whose test is already green
# at the parent fails its proof (exit 1, nothing written); a fix outside the
# allowed roots is skipped; usage errors are exit 2.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  SEED="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/seed-bugfix-tasks.sh"
  VS="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/validate-suite.sh"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sb.XXXXXX")"
  G="$T/repo"; S="$T/suite"
  export LOA_EVAL_PHASE_PROMPTS_DIR="$T/no-prompts"
  python3 -m pytest --version >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "pytest not importable by python3"
  git init -q -b main "$G"
  mkdir -p "$G/tools/mathx/tests" "$G/docs"
  cat > "$G/tools/mathx/rounding.py" <<'PY'
def round_half(x):
    """Round to the nearest integer, halves away from zero."""
    return int(x + 0.5)
PY
  cat > "$G/tools/mathx/tests/conftest.py" <<'PY'
import os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".."))
PY
  cat > "$G/tools/mathx/tests/test_rounding.py" <<'PY'
from rounding import round_half

def test_positive():
    assert round_half(2.5) == 3
PY
  echo "notes" > "$G/docs/README"
  gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "chore: initial"
}

teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }

gc() { git -C "$G" -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t -c commit.gpgsign=false "$@"; }

# the clean fix: negative halves round away from zero; two new test cases
commit_clean_fix() {
  cat > "$G/tools/mathx/rounding.py" <<'PY'
import math


def round_half(x):
    """Round to the nearest integer, halves away from zero."""
    return int(math.copysign(math.floor(abs(x) + 0.5), x))
PY
  cat >> "$G/tools/mathx/tests/test_rounding.py" <<'PY'

def test_negative_half():
    assert round_half(-2.5) == -3

def test_negative():
    assert round_half(-1.6) == -2
PY
  gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "fix(mathx): negative halves round away from zero"
}

commit_claude_fix() {
  mkdir -p "$G/.claude"
  echo 'echo hi' > "$G/.claude/x.sh"
  printf '\ndef test_again():\n    assert round_half(1.5) == 2\n' >> "$G/tools/mathx/tests/test_rounding.py"
  gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "fix: the framework hook"
}

@test "SB-1 a clean fix commit becomes a task: fixture from the parent, hidden tests from the commit, proof printed, validate-suite passes" {
  commit_clean_fix
  FIX="$(git -C "$G" rev-parse HEAD)"; BASE="$(git -C "$G" rev-parse HEAD~1)"
  run "$SEED" --since 2000-01-01 --select 4 --out "$S" --repo "$G"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

content.text:
My verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. The review is in `/workspace/review.md`: eight findings, three of them in the shipped code. I didn't run the bats suites, because most of the files they need aren't in `pr/`. I reproduced the first bug below by hand.

**Blocking problems:**
1. **One failed proof breaks every task after it** (`lib/seed_tasks.py:373`). When a candidate fails its proof or is refused for a secret, its half-built directory stays in the shared staging area. The same task id is then reused, so the next candidate crashes with `File exists`. I built a small repo with an "already green" fix followed by a valid fix: 0 tasks were written, both were reported as proof-failed, and the exit code was 1. The refactor seeder has the same problem at line 450.
2. **Skipped refactor candidates still use up `--select` slots** (`lib/seed_tasks.py:570`). The candidate list is cut to N before anything is built. So a commit that is skipped for having no covering test, or refused for a secret, takes a slot, and the next candidate is never tried. Both script headers say skips and refusals don't count. Test SR-4 only passes because it uses `--select 1` with the skipped commit newest.
3. **A skipped or xfailed pytest case makes the suite count as failing** (`ablation-grade.sh:588`). The grader adds skipped and xfailed tests to the total but not to the passed count, so a suite with one skip never counts as all-passing. That throws off verdict accuracy and the reference self-check. Bats skips, by contrast, count as passes.

**Test assertions that can never fail:**
- In bats, a `! cmd` line that isn't the last line of a test doesn't fail the test, and `a && b` only checks its last part. Because of this, the new "nothing hidden leaked into the sandbox" checks in `pipeline-run.bats` (lines 498, 503, 494) are partly or entirely unenforced.
- The same applies to AG-12's "grade.json carries ids only" checks in `ablation-grade.bats:501`.
- The fix is `|| false` or `run !`, which these files already use in other places.

**Checked and fine:**
- The "generated files are never fix regions" filter. The regenerated pr-14 and pr-15 manifests no longer contain any generated paths (9 and 32 regions removed), and their new checksums match `SHA256SUMS`.
- The new `source.churn` validation.
